'''''Cyclamen coum''''', the '''eastern sowbread''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Primulaceae]]. It is a [[tuber]]ous [[herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]], growing to {{convert|5|-|8|cm|0|abbr=on}}, with rounded heart-shaped leaves and pink shell-shaped flowers with darker coloration at the base. It is valued in horticulture as [[groundcover]], and for the flowers which bloom in winter and early spring.<ref>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z Encyclopedia of Garden Plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref>

==Description==
The [[tuber]] produces [[root]]s from the center of the bottom only.<ref>[http://www.srgc.org.uk/bulblog/log2008/300708/log.html "BULB LOG 31 --- 30th July 2008"] (photos of a tuber). Scottish Rock Garden Club.</ref> It remains small, only reaching about {{convert|6.5|cm|in|abbr=on}} across.

The leaves are round or kidney-shaped to long heart-shaped. The color is all-silver, all-green, or silver [[variegation#Reflective|variegated]] with a variably sized green hastate ([[arrowhead]]-shaped) or "[[Christmas tree]]" pattern and a green edge. The [[leaf#Edge|edge]] is smooth or gently toothed, but never angled and pointed as in ''[[Cyclamen hederifolium]]''.{{cn|date=November 2023}}

The flowers are squat, with almost round [[petal]]s, unlike any other group of cyclamen species. They bloom from winter to spring. The petals are magenta, pink, or white, with a darker blotch at the base. Below the blotch is a small white or pink "eye".{{cn|date=November 2023}}

==Etymology==
The species name ''coum'' more likely refers to Koa or [[Quwê]] (an ancient region in eastern [[Cilicia]], southeastern [[Turkey]]), which is part of the species' natural range, than to the island of [[Kos]], where the species does not grow.<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20050207135414/http://www.paghat.com/cyclamencoum5b.html ''Cyclamen coum'' subsp. ''coum'' Pink Silverleaf]}} at {{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20020810130952/http://paghat.com/ Paghat's Garden]}}</ref>

==Distribution==
''Cyclamen coum'' is [[native plant|native]] to two areas. The main range is around the [[Black Sea]], from [[Bulgaria]] through northern Turkey to the [[Caucasus]] and [[Crimea]], and a disjunct population lies near the Mediterranean from the Hatay Province in Turkey through Lebanon to northern [[Israel]].{{cn|date=November 2023}}

''Cyclamen coum'' subsp. ''coum'' inhabits the western part of the main range and the southern area, while ''C. coum'' subsp. ''caucasicum'' inhabits the eastern part, including the Caucasus. Plants with intermediate characteristics are found in the middle of the range.{{cn|date=November 2023}}

==Cultivation==
''Cyclamen coum'' self-seeds and grows more slowly than ''[[Cyclamen hederifolium]]'' and is usually out-competed when the two are grown together. The species ''C. coum''<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Cyclamen coum''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/5135/Cyclamen-coum/Details | accessdate=15 April 2020}}</ref> and the [[form (botany)|form]] ''C. coum'' subsp. ''coum'' f. ''coum'' Pewter Group<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''C. coum'' subsp. ''coum'' f. ''coum'' Pewter Group|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/98751/Cyclamen-coum-subsp-coum-f-coum-Pewter-Group/Details | accessdate=15 April 2020}}</ref> have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]] (confirmed 2017).<ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 22 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 24 January 2018}}</ref>

===Hardiness===
Along with ''C. hederifolium'' and ''[[Cyclamen purpurascens|C. purpurascens]]'', ''C. coum'' is one of the hardiest cyclamen species, growing well in an area of New York where the temperature has reached as low as {{convert|-19|F|C|0}}.

==Subspecies and forms==
There are two [[subspecies]] and three [[form (botany)|forms]], distinguished by leaf and flower characteristics. ''[[Cyclamen elegans]]'' was formerly considered a subspecies (''Cyclamen coum'' subsp. ''elegans''), but is now a species in its own right.{{cn|date=November 2023}}
* leaf as wide or broader than long
** ''Cyclamen coum'' subsp. ''coum'' (west and south) — leaf edge usually smooth, petal lobes {{convert|0.8|-|1.4|cm|in|1|abbr=on}}
*** ''Cyclamen coum'' subsp. ''coum'' f. ''coum'' — petals pink to magenta, with dark markings at base of petal lobe
*** ''Cyclamen coum'' subsp. ''coum'' f. ''pallidum'' — petals white or very pale pink, with dark markings
*** ''Cyclamen coum'' subsp. ''coum'' f. ''albissimum'' — petals pure white, without markings
* leaf longer than wide
** ''Cyclamen coum'' subsp. ''caucasicum'' (east) — leaf wavy-edged — petals {{convert|1.2|-|2|cm|in|1|abbr=on}}

'''Note:''' The isolate population of Crimea, formerly called ''Cyclamen kuznetzovii'' Kotov & Czernova, is now considered as a local variant of ''Cyclamen coum''.<ref>{{cite journal |first=Andriy V. |last=Yena |year=2007 |journal=Fritschiana |title=Floristic endemism in the Crimea |volume=55 |pages=1–8 |url=https://static.uni-graz.at/fileadmin/nawi-institute/Botanik/Fritschiana/fritschiana-55/fritschiana-55.pdf }}</ref><ref>Janis Ruksans, ''Buried Treasures: Finding and Growing the World's Choicest Bulbs'', p. 113, Timber Press, 2007 - {{ISBN|0-88192-818-6}}</ref>

==Similar species==
The ''Cyclamen coum'' group also includes ''Cyclamen abchasicum'', ''Cyclamen elegans'', ''Cyclamen alpinum'', ''Cyclamen parviflorum'' and ''Cyclamen pseudibericum''.
* leaves wider than long
** ''[[Cyclamen parviflorum]]''
**: flowers tiny; leaves green
* leaves longer than wide; leaf edge coarsely toothed, scalloped, or shallowly lobed
** petals as long as ''Cyclamen coum''
*** ''[[Cyclamen alpinum]]'' (formerly ''Cyclamen trochopteranthum'')
**: petals horizontal, twisted like a propeller; leaves speckled with grey
** petals longer than ''Cyclamen coum''
*** ''[[Cyclamen abchasicum]]'' (formerly ''Cyclamen coum'' var. ''abchasicum'')
**: taxon between ''Cyclamen coum'' and ''Cyclamen elegans''
*** ''[[Cyclamen elegans]]'' (formerly ''Cyclamen coum'' subsp. ''elegans'')
*** ''[[Cyclamen pseudibericum]]''
**: petals with broad dark blotch and white band on nose

==Hybrid==
''Cyclamen'' ×''drydenii'' Grey-Wilson, a hybrid ''Cyclamen coum'' × ''Cyclamen alpinum'', has intermediate characteristics, i.e., round leaves and horizontal twisted petals.
